messages:
carla_onprem: Hey team — customer running Redwood Private in a VPC. Their onboarding hit a wall: model pulls + package installs failing after we enabled strict egress. Getting TLS errors and some auth 401s from model registry. Can we confirm the minimal allowlist for on-prem/air-gapped installs?

ben_support: Thanks Carla. Can you paste the exact error they're seeing? Also what's the OS/container runtime and whether they have a corporate proxy?

carla_onprem: Error log from deploy agent: `ERROR: requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1007)` then subsequent `401 Unauthorized` when hitting model auth at `https://models.redwood.ai/v1/auth`

dave_network: Likely two things: (1) OCSP / CA chain blocked by TLS inspection, (2) outbound to auth/model registry endpoints blocked or rewritten by proxy. Which hosts are they allowing right now?

carla_onprem: They only allowed pypi.org and docker hub so far. No KMS or telemetry hosts.

alice_devex: Quick checklist we send customers — recommend allowing these egress destinations for private installs: `models.redwood.ai` (443), `auth.redwood.ai` (443), `artifacts.redwood-infra.com` (443) for model blobs, `pypi.org` and `files.pythonhosted.org` (443) for pip deps, `ghcr.io` (443) for docker layers, `telemetry.redwood.ai` (443) optionally, and AWS KMS endpoints (regional) for KMS-backed key stores. Also allow OCSP/CRL endpoints for CA chains: e.g., `ocsp.digicert.com` and `crl3.digicert.com` etc.

ben_support: We should give a compact allowlist + recommended tests. Suggest adding: 
```
models.redwood.ai:443
auth.redwood.ai:443
artifacts.redwood-infra.com:443
pypi.org:443
files.pythonhosted.org:443
ghcr.io:443
telemetry.redwood.ai:443
kms.us-west-2.amazonaws.com:443  # replace with customer's region
ocsp.digicert.com:80
crl3.digicert.com:80
```

dave_network: Note: OCSP often uses port 80. If they have transparent TLS inspection, ensure it preserves SNI and doesn't present a custom CA that breaks OCSP stapling. If TLS inspection is unavoidable, they need to add our CA to their trust store or exempt `models.redwood.ai`.

carla_onprem: I ran curl from their host to models endpoint and got `curl: (60) SSL: certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate`. They are using Ubuntu 22.04 in containers.

alice_devex: Repro steps for them to run and share output: 
1) `curl -v https://models.redwood.ai/v1/health`
2) `openssl s_client -connect models.redwood.ai:443 -showcerts -servername models.redwood.ai`
3) `curl -v --proxy <proxy> https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/token` if behind proxy
Share the `openssl` chain and the final `verify return:...` lines.

ben_support: Also request `system ca list` output: `ls -l /etc/ssl/certs` and `update-ca-certificates --verbose` inside the container. Common issue: minimal container images missing ca-certificates package.

infra-bot: Deploy-checker: run `redwoodctl diagnose --collect=network,certs,env` and paste the bundle URL.

carla_onprem: Customer ran `openssl s_client` and their chain is missing the intermediate CA — looks like the inspection device trimmed the chain. They can either disable chain truncation or we can ask to allow direct egress so the client sees full chain from our origin.

dave_network: For firewall rules, give them IP ranges? We prefer hostnames but if they need CIDR we can provide approximate ranges per cloud region. Ask for preferred region and we'll return numeric ranges.

carla_onprem: Customer region is `us-west-2`. I've asked them to temporarily open hostnames and run the `redwoodctl` diag. Also asked for proxy config and docker daemon `--registry-mirror` settings.

ben_support: I'll follow up with a short KB snippet they can paste to their security team explaining why OCSP and KMS endpoints are required and the certificate trust implications.

alice_devex: Added a small troubleshooting snippet they can run to test pip + model pull: 
```
# test pip
python -c "import requests; print(requests.get('https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/index.html').status_code)"
# test model pull auth
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://artifacts.redwood-infra.com/models/small/metadata.json
```

carla_onprem: customer confirmed after allowing `models.redwood.ai` and `ocsp.digicert.com` they no longer see the cert error; model pulls still 401. Sent them steps to capture the token request — likely clock skew or missing client creds.

ben_support: Great. If 401 persists, request `curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/introspect` (mask token) and we can check token audience/iss claims. Also confirm system time `date -u`.

carla_onprem: Marking this thread follow-up. Will paste diag bundle when available. :thumbsup:
